claims.text: What the strip looks like The T wave looks “pushed down”: flattened or inverted T waves, ST depression and prominent U waves.
claims.quote: Hypokalaemia creates the illusion that the T wave is “pushed down”, with resultant T-wave flattening/inversion, ST depression, and prominent U waves

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) T waves: flattened
claims.quote: Hypokalemia: Flattened T waves ST depression Prominent U waves Prolonged QT (actually QU) Predisposes to torsades

claims.text: ST segment: depressed
claims.quote: Hypokalemia: Flattened T waves ST depression Prominent U waves Prolonged QT (actually QU) Predisposes to torsades

claims.text: U waves: prominent (best seen in the precordial leads V2–V3)
claims.quote: Prominent U waves (best seen in the precordial leads V2-V3)

claims.text: QT: looks prolonged — it = really the QU interval (T and U waves fused)
claims.quote: Apparent long QT interval due to fusion of T and U waves (= long QU interval)

claims.text: P wave and PR (LITFL lists these @ K < 2.7 mmol/L): taller P waves, longer PR
claims.quote: ECG features of hypokalaemia (K < 2.7 mmol/L) Increased P wave amplitude Prolongation of PR interval

claims.text: Rhythm, as it worsens: freq supraventricular and ventricular ectopics; AF, A-flutter or atrial tachy; potential VT, VF and torsades de pointes
claims.quote: With worsening hypokalaemia… Frequent supraventricular and ventricular ectopics Supraventricular tachyarrhythmias: AF, atrial flutter, atrial tachycardia Potential to develop life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, e.g. VT, VF and Torsades de Pointes

claims.text: Conduction: may cause second- or third-degree AV block; eventually VF may occur
claims.quote: Hypokalemia may cause premature ventricular and atrial contractions, ventricular and atrial tachyarrhythmias, and second- or third-degree atrioventricular block; eventually, ventricular fibrillation may occur.

claims.text: When it shows: ♡ effects are USU minimal until potassium = < 3 mEq/L
claims.quote: Cardiac effects of hypokalemia are usually minimal until serum potassium concentrations are < 3 mEq/L (< 3 mmol/L).

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: ↓extracell potassium makes the myocardium hyperexcitable, w the potential for re-entrant arrhythmias
claims.quote: Decreased extracellular potassium causes myocardial hyperexcitability with the potential to develop re-entrant arrhythmias.

claims.text: Eti: ↓intake or a shift of potassium into cells, but USU excessive losses in the urine or from the GI tract
claims.quote: Hypokalemia can be caused by decreased intake of potassium or shift of extracellular potassium into cells, but it is usually caused by excessive losses of potassium in the urine or from the gastrointestinal tract.

claims.text: Diuretics are by far the MC med cause
claims.quote: Diuretics are by far the most commonly used medications that cause hypokalemia.

claims.text: Shift into cells: after insulin, familial periodic paralysis, glycogenesis during parenteral or enteral nutrition, β 2-agonists (ex, albuterol, terbutaline), and occasionally thyrotoxicosis
claims.quote: This shift can occur in any of the following: After administration of insulin Familial periodic paralysis Glycogenesis during parenteral nutrition or enteral hyperalimentation (stimulating insulin release) Stimulation of the sympathetic nervous system, particularly with beta 2-agonists (eg, albuterol, terbutaline), which may increase cellular potassium uptake Thyrotoxicosis (occasionally)

claims.text: Often w ↓magnesium, which raises the risk of malig ventricular arrhythmias
claims.quote: Hypokalaemia is often associated with hypomagnesaemia, which increases the risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias

claims.text: Sx Mild (3.0 to 3.4 mEq/L): rarely → Sx
claims.quote: Mild hypokalemia (serum potassium 3.0 to 3.4 mEq/L [3.0 to 3.4 mmol/L]) rarely causes symptoms.

claims.text: Mod (2.5 to 3.0 mEq/L): generally musc weakness; may lead to paralysis and resp failure
claims.quote: Moderate hypokalemia (serum potassium 2.5 to 3.0 mEq/L [2.5 to 3.0 mmol/L]) generally causes muscle weakness and may lead to paralysis and respiratory failure.

claims.text: Severe (< 2.5 mEq/L): ECG chgs or severe Sx
claims.quote: Severe hypokalemia (< 2.5 mEq/L [< 2.5 mmol/L]) causes ECG changes or severe symptoms.

claims.text: Other musc effects: cramping, fasciculations, paralytic ileus, hypovent, hypotension, tetany, and rhabdomyolysis
claims.quote: Other muscular dysfunction includes cramping, fasciculations, paralytic ileus, hypoventilation, hypotension, tetany, and rhabdomyolysis.

claims.text: Tx Oral potassium supplements; IV potassium for severe hypokalemia or ongoing losses
claims.quote: Oral potassium supplements IV potassium supplements for severe hypokalemia or ongoing potassium losses

claims.text: Give it IV when severe (ex, ECG chgs or severe Sx), unresponsive to oral therapy, or in hsp pts taking digoxin or w sig Hdz or ongoing losses
claims.quote: When hypokalemia is severe (eg, with ECG changes or severe symptoms), is unresponsive to oral therapy, or occurs in hospitalized patients who are taking digoxin or who have significant heart disease or ongoing losses, potassium must be replaced IV.

claims.text: IV limits: concentration should ⍉exceed 40 mEq/L (v. irritate); routine infusion rate should ⍉exceed 10 mEq/hr
claims.quote: Because potassium solutions can irritate peripheral veins, the concentration should not exceed 40 mEq/L (40 mmol/L). The rate of correction of hypokalemia is limited because of the lag in potassium movement from the extracellular space into cells. Routine infusion rates should not exceed 10 mEq (10 mmol)/hour.

claims.text: Hypokalemia-induced arrhythmia: IV KCl faster, USU thru a central v. or several periph veins; 40 mEq/hr only w cont ♡ monitoring and hourly potassium levels
claims.quote: In hypokalemia-induced arrhythmia, IV potassium chloride must be given more rapidly, usually through a central vein or using multiple peripheral veins simultaneously. Infusion of 40 mEq (40 mmol) potassium chloride/hour can be undertaken but only with continuous cardiac monitoring and hourly serum potassium determinations.

claims.text: W ↓magnesium: correct both potassium and magnesium, to stop ongoing renal potassium wasting
claims.quote: When hypokalemia occurs with hypomagnesemia, both the potassium and magnesium deficiencies must be corrected to stop ongoing renal potassium wasting.

claims.text: Strd practice in most CCUs and ICUs: replace potassium to ≥ 4.0 mmol/L and magnesium to ≥ 1.0 mmol/L to stabilize the myocardium and protect against arrhythmias
claims.quote: Replace potassium to ≥ 4.0 mmol/L and magnesium to ≥ 1.0 mmol/L to stabilise the myocardium and protect against arrhythmias – this is standard practice in most CCUs and ICUs
